See Squished's reply above. Definitely make at least one jar of them. Searching "fermented lemons" also turns up a lot of recipes.

You can do in salt water or their own juice. There is also a Chinese method that you can do it in herbs. If you need a long shelf life they need to be submerged in a brine.

  • Take container - non metal
  • Put salt in bottom of container.
  • Rinse fruit with out soap or salt. Remove mold and brown spots. Cut off ends.

  • I cut them into wedges (peel and all). You can just cut them star fashion and stuff salt in the center then stuff them in the container.

  • Top off with water if you went the stuffed route. Or use 1 TBSP salt for each cup water if you went wedges or slices.

Takes about a month to ferment. If you have a starter use it. Sweeter lemons will try to mold on you and may need more salt.

Note on water: use distilled (buy in baby section of stores) because city water tends to kill ferments. Rainwater gives the most stable ferment though.

  • For amount of lemons (or limes) to start with,. Stuff 1 pound of lemons in a pint container.

  • Ferments want to be around 75°F. If you want to enjoy chilled fermented lemon, you can put them in the fridge but they need to finish fermenting first.

I think starting with limes is good for a first timer because they actually change color when they start fermenting. Ferment is done when peel is soft and non-bitter. Don't sweat the slime.
